subject: prog-cont
title: PROG.CONT.-----TR.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-40 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan) accompanying Braxton's closing claim about world creativity: 'the real dynamics of world transformation will be directly proportioned to how individuals deal with the challenge of actual reality expansion — both theoretically and actually.' PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) is crossed with TR (transformation): the question is what progressional-continuance produces when crossed with transformation — under conditions where individual transcultural artistic activity is the operative scale. CRTF-D (creative-dynamic) sits between subject and partner. TR is partner-center. INFO-DE (information descent) sits centrally on the right. (R)PART (the reality of participation) anchors the upper-right margin via a *dashed* edge — conditional. T-C-IMP (temporal-continuity implication) sits below the central axis. AFI (affinity insight) anchors the right output. CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics) feeds in from the lower-left. EXT-F (extended functionalism) sits centrally below. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) anchors the lower-center. BSCF (basic continuance-functionalism) hangs on the lower-right. Structural argument: progressional-continuance crossed with transformation is mediated by creative-dynamic as central hub and temporal-continuity-implication as lower hub. The dashed edge to reality-of-participation is load-bearing: world-transformation produces real participation only conditionally — the individual transcultural artist (Tony Scott, Akiyoshi, Watanabe in the surrounding prose) must actively hold that edge. The diagram is Braxton's structural case for why individual world-musicianship matters: it is the only configuration in which the conditional participation edge gets actively maintained, producing affinity-insight and basic-continuance-functionalism as the real outputs of progressional-continuance crossed with transformation.
